```
    44→    def clusters_updated(self) -> int:
    45→        return self.epics_updated
    46→
    47→    @property
    48→    def clusters_completed(self) -> int:
    49→        return self.epics_completed
    50→
    51→
    52→def _epic_sort_key(epic_data: dict) -> int:
    53→    return int(epic_data.get("dependency_order", 999))
    54→
    55→
    56→def _normalized_epic_name(raw_name: str) -> str:
    57→    return raw_name if raw_name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX) else f"{EPIC_PREFIX}{raw_name}"
    58→
    59→
    60→def _update_existing_epic_cluster(
    61→    existing: Cluster,
    62→    epic_data: dict,
    63→    *,
    64→    now: str,
    65→    version: int,
    66→) -> None:
    67→    existing["thesis"] = epic_data["thesis"]
    68→    existing["direction"] = epic_data["direction"]
    69→    existing["root_cause"] = epic_data.get("root_cause", "")
    70→    existing["issue_ids"] = epic_data["issue_ids"]
    71→    existing["dismissed"] = epic_data.get("dismissed", [])
    72→    existing["agent_safe"] = epic_data.get("agent_safe", False)
    73→    existing["dependency_order"] = epic_data["dependency_order"]
    74→    existing["action_steps"] = epic_data.get("action_steps", [])
    75→    existing["execution_status"] = EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE
    76→    existing["updated_at"] = now
    77→    existing["triage_version"] = version
    78→    existing["description"] = epic_data["thesis"]
    79→    # Don't overwrite in_progress status from agent
    80→    if existing.get("status") != "in_progress":
    81→        existing["status"] = epic_data.get("status", "pending")
    82→
    83→
    84→def _create_epic_cluster(
    85→    *,
    86→    epic_name: str,
    87→    epic_data: dict,
    88→    now: str,
    89→    version: int,
    90→) -> Cluster:
    91→    return {
    92→        "name": epic_name,
    93→        "description": epic_data["thesis"],
    94→        "issue_ids": epic_data["issue_ids"],
    95→        "auto": True,
    96→        "cluster_key": f"epic::{epic_name}",
    97→        "action": f"desloppify plan focus {epic_name}",
    98→        "execution_status": EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE,
    99→        "user_modified": False,
   100→        "created_at": now,
   101→        "updated_at": now,
   102→        # Epic fields
   103→        "thesis": epic_data["thesis"],
   104→        "direction": epic_data["direction"],
   105→        "root_cause": epic_data.get("root_cause", ""),
   106→        "supersedes": [],
   107→        "dismissed": epic_data.get("dismissed", []),
   108→        "agent_safe": epic_data.get("agent_safe", False),
   109→        "dependency_order": epic_data["dependency_order"],
   110→        "action_steps": epic_data.get("action_steps", []),
   111→        "source_clusters": [],
   112→        "status": epic_data.get("status", "pending"),
   113→        "triage_version": version,
   114→    }
   115→
   116→
   117→def _upsert_triage_clusters(
   118→    *,
   119→    clusters: dict[str, Cluster],
   120→    triage: TriageResult,
   121→    now: str,
   122→    version: int,
   123→) -> tuple[int, int]:
   124→    created = 0
   125→    updated = 0
   126→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   127→        raw_name = epic_data["name"]
   128→        epic_name = _normalized_epic_name(raw_name)
   129→        existing = clusters.get(epic_name)
   130→        if existing and existing.get("thesis"):
   131→            _update_existing_epic_cluster(existing, epic_data, now=now, version=version)
   132→            updated += 1
   133→            continue
   134→        clusters[epic_name] = _create_epic_cluster(
   135→            epic_name=epic_name,
   136→            epic_data=epic_data,
   137→            now=now,
   138→            version=version,
   139→        )
   140→        created += 1
   141→    return created, updated
   142→
   143→
   144→def _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   145→    *,
   146→    order: list[str],
   147→    triage: TriageResult,
   148→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   149→) -> None:
   150→    epic_issue_ids: set[str] = set()
   151→    epic_ordered_ids: list[str] = []
   152→    dismissed_set = set(dismissed_ids)
   153→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   154→        for fid in epic_data["issue_ids"]:
   155→            if fid in epic_issue_ids or fid in dismissed_set:
   156→                continue
   157→            epic_issue_ids.add(fid)
   158→            epic_ordered_ids.append(fid)
   159→
   160→    non_epic_items = [fid for fid in order if fid not in epic_issue_ids]
   161→    order.clear()
   162→    order.extend(epic_ordered_ids)
   163→    order.extend(non_epic_items)
   164→
   165→
   166→def _set_triage_meta(
   167→    *,
   168→    plan: PlanModel,
   169→    state: StateModel,
   170→    triage: TriageResult,
   171→    now: str,
   172→    version: int,
   173→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   174→    trigger: str,
   175→) -> None:
   176→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   177→    open_review_ids = sorted(
   178→        fid
   179→        for fid, issue in (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {})).items()
   180→        if issue.get("status") == "open"
   181→        and is_triage_finding(issue)
   182→    )
   183→
   184→    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = {
   185→        "triaged_ids": open_review_ids,
   186→        "last_run": now,
   187→        "version": version,
   188→        "dismissed_ids": dismissed_ids,
   189→        "issue_snapshot_hash": current_hash,
   190→        "strategy_summary": triage.strategy_summary,
   191→        "trigger": trigger,
   192→    }
   193→
   194→
   195→def _apply_auto_cluster_decisions(
   196→    *,
   197→    plan: PlanModel,
   198→    decisions: list[AutoClusterDecision],
   199→    order: list[str],
   200→    now: str,
   201→    version: int,
   202→    result: TriageMutationResult,
   203→) -> None:
   204→    """Process auto_cluster_decisions from the triage result.
   205→
   206→    - promote: add cluster issue IDs to queue_order
   207→    - skip: mark the cluster as skipped in the plan
   208→    - break_up: record the decision for downstream processing
   209→    """
   210→    clusters = plan["clusters"]
   211→
   212→    for decision in decisions:
   213→        cluster_name = decision.cluster
   214→        cluster = clusters.get(cluster_name)
   215→        if cluster is None:
   216→            continue
   217→
   218→        action = decision.action
   219→
   220→        if action == "promote":
   221→            issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   222→            existing_in_order = set(order)
   223→            new_ids = [
   224→                fid for fid in issue_ids
   225→                if isinstance(fid, str) and fid not in existing_in_order
   226→            ]
   227→            # Determine insertion position based on priority hint
   228→            priority = (decision.priority or "").lower().strip()
   229→            if priority == "first":
   230→                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):
   231→                    order.insert(i, fid)
   232→            elif priority.startswith("after "):
   233→                target = priority[len("after "):]
   234→                insert_idx = len(order)
   235→                for idx, item in enumerate(order):
   236→                    if target in item:
   237→                        insert_idx = idx + 1
   238→                        break
   239→                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):
   240→                    order.insert(insert_idx + i, fid)
   241→            elif priority.startswith("before "):
   242→                target = priority[len("before "):]
   243→                insert_idx = len(order)
   244→                for idx, item in enumerate(order):
   245→                    if target in item:
   246→                        insert_idx = idx
   247→                        break
   248→                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):
   249→                    order.insert(insert_idx + i, fid)
   250→            else:
   251→                # "last" or unrecognized: append to end
   252→                order.extend(new_ids)
   253→
   254→            cluster["execution_status"] = EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE
   255→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   256→            cluster["triage_version"] = version
   257→            result.auto_clusters_promoted += 1
   258→
   259→        elif action == "skip":
   260→            cluster["triage_skip"] = {
   261→                "reason": decision.reason,
   262→                "skipped_at": now,
   263→                "triage_version": version,
   264→            }
   265→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   266→            result.auto_clusters_skipped += 1
   267→
   268→        elif action == "break_up":
   269→            cluster["triage_break_up"] = {
   270→                "reason": decision.reason,
   271→                "sub_clusters": decision.sub_clusters,
   272→                "decided_at": now,
   273→                "triage_version": version,
   274→            }
   275→            cluster["updated_at"] = now
   276→            result.auto_clusters_broken_up += 1
   277→
   278→
   279→def apply_triage_to_plan(
   280→    plan: PlanModel,
   281→    state: StateModel,
   282→    triage: TriageResult,
   283→    *,
   284→    trigger: str = "manual",
   285→) -> TriageMutationResult:
   286→    """Apply parsed triage result to the living plan.
   287→
   288→    1. Creates/updates triage clusters in plan["clusters"]
   289→    2. Marks dismissed issues as triaged_out skips
   290→    3. Reorders queue_order to group cluster members by dependency_order
   291→    4. Updates epic_triage_meta with snapshot hash
   292→    """
   293→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   294→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   295→    now = utc_now()
   296→    result = TriageMutationResult()
   297→    result.strategy_summary = triage.strategy_summary
   298→
   299→    clusters = plan["clusters"]
   300→    skipped: dict = plan["skipped"]
   301→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   302→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   303→    version = int(meta.get("version", 0)) + 1
   304→    result.triage_version = version
   305→
   306→    created, updated = _upsert_triage_clusters(
   307→        clusters=clusters,
   308→        triage=triage,
   309→        now=now,
   310→        version=version,
   311→    )
   312→    result.epics_created += created
   313→    result.epics_updated += updated
   314→
   315→    dismissed_ids, dismiss_count = dismiss_triage_issues(
   316→        triage=triage,
   317→        order=order,
   318→        skipped=skipped,
   319→        now=now,
   320→        version=version,
   321→        scan_count=int(state.get("scan_count", 0)),
   322→    )
   323→    result.issues_dismissed += dismiss_count
   324→
   325→    # Sync state status for dismissed issues so state is authoritative.
   326→    issues = (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {}))
   327→    triaged_out_status = skip_kind_state_status("triaged_out")
   328→    for fid in dismissed_ids:
   329→        issue = issues.get(fid)
   330→        if issue and issue.get("status") == "open" and triaged_out_status:
   331→            issue["status"] = triaged_out_status
   332→            issue["note"] = f"Triaged out by epic triage v{version}"
   333→
   334→    _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   335→        order=order,
   336→        triage=triage,
   337→        dismissed_ids=dismissed_ids,
   338→    )
   339→
   340→    # Process auto-cluster decisions (backward-compatible: no-op if empty)
   341→    if triage.auto_cluster_decisions:
   342→        _apply_auto_cluster_decisions(
   343→            plan=plan,
   344→            decisions=triage.auto_cluster_decisions,
   345→            order=order,
   346→            now=now,
   347→            version=version,
   348→            result=result,
   349→        )
   350→
   351→    _set_triage_meta(
   352→        plan=plan,
   353→        state=state,
   354→        triage=triage,
   355→        now=now,
   356→        version=version,
   357→        dismissed_ids=dismissed_ids,
   358→        trigger=trigger,
   359→    )
   360→    plan["updated"] = now
   361→
   362→    return result
   363→
   364→__all__ = ["TriageMutationResult", "apply_triage_to_plan"]
   365→
```

```
1→"""Canonical cluster mutations for plan operations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._plan.cluster_semantics import (
     6→    ACTION_TYPE_MANUAL_FIX,
     7→    EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE,
     8→    EXECUTION_POLICY_PLANNED_ONLY,
     9→)
    10→from desloppify.engine._plan.operations.lifecycle import clear_focus_if_cluster_empty
    11→from desloppify.engine._plan.operations.queue import move_items
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import Cluster, PlanModel, ensure_plan_defaults
    13→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    14→
    15→
    16→def _cluster_or_raise(plan: PlanModel, cluster_name: str) -> Cluster:
    17→    cluster = plan["clusters"].get(cluster_name)
    18→    if cluster is None:
    19→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist")
    20→    return cluster
    21→
    22→
    23→def _upsert_cluster_override(
    24→    plan: PlanModel,
    25→    issue_id: str,
    26→    *,
    27→    cluster_name: str,
    28→    timestamp: str,
    29→) -> None:
    30→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
    31→    if issue_id not in overrides:
    32→        overrides[issue_id] = {"issue_id": issue_id, "created_at": timestamp}
    33→    overrides[issue_id]["cluster"] = cluster_name
    34→    overrides[issue_id]["updated_at"] = timestamp
    35→
    36→
    37→def _clear_cluster_override(
    38→    plan: PlanModel,
    39→    issue_id: str,
    40→    *,
    41→    cluster_name: str,
    42→    timestamp: str,
    43→) -> None:
    44→    override = plan["overrides"].get(issue_id)
    45→    if override and override.get("cluster") == cluster_name:
    46→        override["cluster"] = None
    47→        override["updated_at"] = timestamp
    48→
    49→
    50→def _copy_missing_cluster_metadata(target: Cluster, source: Cluster) -> None:
    51→    if not target.get("description") and source.get("description"):
    52→        target["description"] = source["description"]
    53→    if not target.get("action_steps") and source.get("action_steps"):
    54→        target["action_steps"] = list(source["action_steps"])
    55→    if not target.get("action") and source.get("action"):
    56→        target["action"] = source["action"]
    57→
    58→
    59→def create_cluster(
    60→    plan: PlanModel,
    61→    name: str,
    62→    description: str | None = None,
    63→    action: str | None = None,
    64→) -> Cluster:
    65→    """Create a named cluster. Raises ValueError if it already exists."""
    66→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    67→    if name.startswith("auto/"):
    68→        raise ValueError(
    69→            f"Cluster names starting with 'auto/' are reserved for auto-clusters: {name!r}"
    70→        )
    71→    if name.startswith("epic/"):
    72→        raise ValueError(
    73→            f"Cluster names starting with 'epic/' are reserved for triage epics: {name!r}"
    74→        )
    75→    if name in plan["clusters"]:
    76→        raise ValueError(f"Cluster {name!r} already exists")
    77→    now = utc_now()
    78→    cluster: Cluster = {
    79→        "name": name,
    80→        "description": description,
    81→        "issue_ids": [],
    82→        "created_at": now,
    83→        "updated_at": now,
    84→        "auto": False,
    85→        "cluster_key": "",
    86→        "action": action,
    87→        "action_type": ACTION_TYPE_MANUAL_FIX,
    88→        "execution_policy": EXECUTION_POLICY_PLANNED_ONLY,
    89→        "execution_status": EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE,
    90→        "user_modified": False,
    91→    }
    92→    plan["clusters"][name] = cluster
    93→    return cluster
    94→
    95→
    96→def add_to_cluster(
    97→    plan: PlanModel,
    98→    cluster_name: str,
    99→    issue_ids: list[str],
   100→) -> int:
   101→    """Add issue IDs to a cluster. Returns count added."""
   102→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   103→    cluster = _cluster_or_raise(plan, cluster_name)
   104→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["issue_ids"]
   105→    count = 0
   106→    now = utc_now()
   107→    for fid in issue_ids:
   108→        if fid not in member_ids:
   109→            member_ids.append(fid)
   110→            count += 1
   111→        _upsert_cluster_override(
   112→            plan,
   113→            fid,
   114→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   115→            timestamp=now,
   116→        )
   117→
   118→    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   119→    return count
   120→
   121→
   122→def remove_from_cluster(
   123→    plan: PlanModel,
   124→    cluster_name: str,
   125→    issue_ids: list[str],
   126→) -> int:
   127→    """Remove issue IDs from a cluster. Returns count removed."""
   128→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   129→    cluster = _cluster_or_raise(plan, cluster_name)
   130→    member_ids: list[str] = cluster["issue_ids"]
   131→    removed_ids = set(issue_ids)
   132→    now = utc_now()
   133→    count = 0
   134→    for fid in issue_ids:
   135→        if fid in member_ids:
   136→            member_ids.remove(fid)
   137→            count += 1
   138→        _clear_cluster_override(
   139→            plan,
   140→            fid,
   141→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   142→            timestamp=now,
   143→        )
   144→
   145→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps")
   146→    if isinstance(steps, list):
   147→        for step in steps:
   148→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
   149→                continue
   150→            refs = step.get("issue_refs")
   151→            if not isinstance(refs, list):
   152→                continue
   153→            filtered_refs = [
   154→                ref for ref in refs
   155→                if isinstance(ref, str) and ref not in removed_ids
   156→            ]
   157→            if filtered_refs != refs:
   158→                step["issue_refs"] = filtered_refs
   159→
   160→    if count > 0 and cluster.get("auto"):
   161→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   162→
   163→    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   164→    clear_focus_if_cluster_empty(plan)
   165→    return count
   166→
   167→
   168→def delete_cluster(plan: PlanModel, name: str) -> list[str]:
   169→    """Delete a cluster and clear cluster refs from overrides. Returns orphaned IDs."""
   170→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   171→    cluster = _cluster_or_raise(plan, name)
   172→    plan["clusters"].pop(name, None)
   173→
   174→    orphaned = list(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   175→    now = utc_now()
   176→    for fid in orphaned:
   177→        _clear_cluster_override(
   178→            plan,
   179→            fid,
   180→            cluster_name=name,
   181→            timestamp=now,
   182→        )
   183→
   184→    if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   185→        plan["active_cluster"] = None
   186→
   187→    return orphaned
   188→
   189→
   190→def merge_clusters(
   191→    plan: PlanModel,
   192→    source_name: str,
   193→    target_name: str,
   194→) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
   195→    """Move all source issues to target, copy missing metadata, delete source."""
   196→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   197→    if source_name == target_name:
   198→        raise ValueError("Cannot merge a cluster into itself")
   199→    source = _cluster_or_raise(plan, source_name)
   200→    target = _cluster_or_raise(plan, target_name)
   201→
   202→    source_ids = list(source.get("issue_ids", []))
   203→    target_ids: list[str] = target["issue_ids"]
   204→    now = utc_now()
   205→
   206→    existing = set(target_ids)
   207→    added = 0
   208→    for fid in source_ids:
   209→        if fid not in existing:
   210→            target_ids.append(fid)
   211→            existing.add(fid)
   212→            added += 1
   213→        _upsert_cluster_override(
   214→            plan,
   215→            fid,
   216→            cluster_name=target_name,
   217→            timestamp=now,
   218→        )
   219→
   220→    _copy_missing_cluster_metadata(target, source)
   221→
   222→    target["updated_at"] = now
   223→
   224→    plan["clusters"].pop(source_name, None)
   225→    if plan.get("active_cluster") == source_name:
   226→        plan["active_cluster"] = None
   227→
   228→    return added, source_ids
   229→
   230→
   231→def move_cluster(
   232→    plan: PlanModel,
   233→    cluster_name: str,
   234→    position: str,
   235→    target: str | None = None,
   236→    offset: int | None = None,
   237→) -> int:
   238→    """Move all cluster members as a contiguous block. Returns count moved."""
   239→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   240→    cluster = _cluster_or_raise(plan, cluster_name)
   241→    member_ids = list(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   242→    if not member_ids:
   243→        return 0
   244→
   245→    return move_items(plan, member_ids, position, target, offset)
   246→
   247→
   248→__all__ = [
   249→    "add_to_cluster",
   250→    "create_cluster",
   251→    "delete_cluster",
   252→    "merge_clusters",
   253→    "move_cluster",
   254→    "remove_from_cluster",
   255→]
   256→
```

```
    11→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    12→# Lazy import helper — avoids the circular import in resolve/render
    13→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    15→def _import_guard():
    16→    """Import _check_queue_order_guard, patching away the render dependency."""
    17→    import desloppify.app.commands.resolve.cmd as cmd_mod
    18→    return cmd_mod._check_queue_order_guard
    19→
    20→
    21→def _get_guard_fn():
    22→    """Return the guard function, handling circular import gracefully."""
    23→    try:
    24→        return _import_guard()
    25→    except ImportError:
    26→        # Fall back: patch the problematic render import chain
    27→        import sys
    28→        stub = MagicMock()
    29→        modules_to_stub = [
    30→            "desloppify.app.commands.helpers.score_update",
    31→            "desloppify.app.commands.scan.helpers",
    32→        ]
    33→        saved = {}
    34→        for mod_name in modules_to_stub:
    35→            if mod_name in sys.modules:
    36→                saved[mod_name] = sys.modules[mod_name]
    37→            sys.modules[mod_name] = stub
    38→
    39→        # Force reimport
    40→        import desloppify.app.commands.resolve.cmd as cmd_mod
    41→        importlib.reload(cmd_mod)
    42→        fn = cmd_mod._check_queue_order_guard
    43→
    44→        # Restore
    45→        for mod_name in modules_to_stub:
    46→            if mod_name in saved:
    47→                sys.modules[mod_name] = saved[mod_name]
    48→            else:
    49→                sys.modules.pop(mod_name, None)
    50→        return fn
    51→
    52→
    53→_check_queue_order_guard = _get_guard_fn()
```

```
    37→def _find_candidates(
    38→    state: StateModel, detector: str, file: str
    39→) -> list[str]:
    40→    """Find alive issues that could be remaps for a disappeared issue."""
    41→    candidates: list[str] = []
    42→    for fid, issue in (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {})).items():
    43→        if issue.get("status") not in _ALIVE_STATUSES:
    44→            continue
    45→        if issue.get("detector") == detector and issue.get("file") == file:
    46→            candidates.append(fid)
    47→    return candidates
    48→
    49→
    50→_ALIVE_STATUSES = frozenset({"open", "deferred", "triaged_out"})
    51→
    52→
    53→def _is_issue_alive(state: StateModel, issue_id: str) -> bool:
    54→    """Return True if the issue exists and is actionable (open/deferred/triaged_out)."""
    55→    issue = (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {})).get(issue_id)
    56→    if issue is None:
    57→        return False
    58→    return issue.get("status") in _ALIVE_STATUSES
    59→
    60→
    61→def _supersede_id(
    62→    plan: PlanModel,
    63→    state: StateModel,
    64→    issue_id: str,
    65→    now: str,
    66→) -> bool:
    67→    """Move a disappeared issue to superseded. Returns True if changed."""
    68→    issue = (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {})).get(issue_id)
    69→    detector = ""
    70→    file = ""
    71→    summary = ""
    72→    if issue:
    73→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    74→        file = issue.get("file", "")
    75→        summary = issue.get("summary", "")
    76→
    77→    candidates = _find_candidates(state, detector, file) if detector else []
    78→    # Don't include the original in candidates
    79→    candidates = [c for c in candidates if c != issue_id]
    80→
    81→    entry: SupersededEntry = {
    82→        "original_id": issue_id,
    83→        "original_detector": detector,
    84→        "original_file": file,
    85→        "original_summary": summary,
    86→        "status": "superseded",
    87→        "superseded_at": now,
    88→        "remapped_to": None,
    89→        "candidates": candidates[:5],
    90→    }
    91→
    92→    # Preserve any existing override note
    93→    override_note = get_issue_note(plan, issue_id)
    94→    if override_note:

   100→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])

   102→    if issue_id in order:

   104→    skipped.pop(issue_id, None)

   120→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   121→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   122→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   123→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   124→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   125→
   126→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   127→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   128→        try:
   129→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   130→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   131→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   132→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   133→                to_prune.append(fid)
   134→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   135→            to_prune.append(fid)
   136→
   137→    for fid in to_prune:
   138→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   139→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   140→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   141→
   142→    return to_prune
```

```
   277→    """Sync state status for skipped issues that are still 'open'.
   278→
   279→    Ensures state is authoritative: temporary → deferred, triaged_out → triaged_out.

   294→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(

   296→    state: StateModel,
   297→) -> ReconcileResult:
   298→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   299→
   300→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   301→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   302→    """
   303→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   304→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   305→    result = ReconcileResult()
   306→    now = utc_now()
   307→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)

   317→        for name, cluster in clusters.items()
   318→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   319→    }

   321→    # Sync state status for issues in plan.skipped that are still "open" in state.
   322→    # This migrates existing data: temporary skips → deferred, triaged_out skips → triaged_out.
   323→    _sync_skipped_issue_statuses(plan, state)
   324→
   325→    _supersede_dead_references(
   326→        plan,
   327→        state,
   328→        referenced_ids=referenced_ids,
   329→        now=now,

   331→    )
   332→    _complete_empty_manual_clusters(plan, pre_sizes=pre_sizes, result=result)
   333→    _reconcile_epic_clusters(plan, state, result=result)

   346→        for fid in resurfaced:

   348→            if issue and issue.get("status") == "deferred":
```

## Summary: Cluster Creation and queue_order Flow

Based on my thorough investigation of the desloppify codebase, here are the answers to your questions:

### 1. **Does a manual cluster automatically get added to queue_order when created?**

**NO - This is a GAP.** 

When you create a manual cluster with `desloppify plan cluster create`, the cluster is created in `plan["clusters"]` with an empty `issue_ids` list, but **the cluster name itself and its issue_ids are NOT automatically added to queue_order**.

**Evidence:**
- File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/cluster.py`, lines 59-93
- The `create_cluster()` function creates a cluster with `"issue_ids": []` but performs zero queue operations
- When you later add issues to the cluster via `add_to_cluster()`, those issue IDs are added to the cluster's `issue_ids` list but NOT automatically added to `queue_order`

### 2. **How does the cluster creation command work?**

**Command flow:**
1. **Handler**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster/ops_manage.py`, function `_cmd_cluster_create()` (lines 125-157)
2. **Dispatcher**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster/dispatch.py`, function `cmd_cluster_dispatch()` (lines 228-248)
3. **Core operation**: Calls `create_cluster()` from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/cluster.py`
4. **Result**: Cluster is added to `plan["clusters"][name]` with metadata but NO queue changes

### 3. **How does apply_triage_to_plan handle queue_order?**

**apply_triage_to_plan reorders queue_order based on epic cluster issue_ids:**

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/apply.py`, lines 279-362

The function:
1. Creates/updates epic clusters in `plan["clusters"]`
2. Calls `_reorder_queue_by_dependency()` (lines 144-163) which:
   - Extracts all issue_ids from triage clusters in dependency order
   - **ASSUMES those issue_ids are already in queue_order**
   - Reorders queue_order to group epic members together
   - Does NOT add missing issue_ids to queue_order

**Critical code (lines 160-163):**
```python
non_epic_items = [fid for fid in order if fid not in epic_issue_ids]
order.clear()
order.extend(epic_ordered_ids)  # Epic members already in order
order.extend(non_epic_items)
```

This assumes epic issue_ids are pre-existing in queue_order.

### 4. **Is there a gap where clusters get created but their issue_ids don't get added to queue_order?**

**YES - DEFINITE GAP** (for non-epic manual clusters)

**The Gap:**
- When you manually create a cluster and add issues to it, those issues are stored in `cluster["issue_ids"]` but NOT added to `queue_order`
- Issues in a cluster can exist completely outside of `queue_order`
- They won't appear in the work queue until manually moved or unless triage is applied

**Where issue_ids GET added to queue_order normally:**
1. **Review import**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync/review_import.py`, lines 179-186
   - New review issues are appended to `queue_order` when the plan is imported
   
2. **Unskipping**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/skip.py`, lines 141, 167
   - Resurfaced skipped issues are appended to `queue_order`
   
3. **Triage application**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/apply.py`, lines 220-252
   - Epic triage clusters can PROMOTE cluster members into `queue_order` via auto-cluster decisions
   
4. **Manual reordering**: Various `move_items()` operations

**For manual clusters:** There's no automatic mechanism to ensure cluster issue_ids are in queue_order.

### Key Files Referenced:
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/cluster.py` - Core cluster operations
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster/ops_manage.py` - CLI cluster create handler

```
   100→def cleanup_image_cache(max_age_hours: int = 24) -> int:
   101→    """
   102→    Delete cached images older than *max_age_hours*.
   103→
   104→    Returns the number of files removed.
   105→    """
   106→    import time
   107→
   108→    cache_dir = get_image_cache_dir()
   109→    cutoff = time.time() - (max_age_hours * 3600)
   110→    removed = 0
   111→    for f in cache_dir.iterdir():
   112→        if f.is_file() and f.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:
   113→            try:
   114→                f.unlink()
   115→                removed += 1
   116→            except OSError:
   117→                pass
   118→    return removed
   119→

   121→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   122→# Audio cache utilities
   123→#
   124→# Same pattern as image cache -- voice messages from platforms are downloaded
   125→# here so the STT tool (OpenAI Whisper) can transcribe them from local files.
   126→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   127→
   128→AUDIO_CACHE_DIR = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/audio_cache"))
   129→
   130→
   131→def get_audio_cache_dir() -> Path:
   132→    """Return the audio cache directory, creating it if it doesn't exist."""
   133→    AUDIO_CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   134→    return AUDIO_CACHE_DIR
   135→
   136→
   137→def cache_audio_from_bytes(data: bytes, ext: str = ".ogg") -> str:
   138→    """
   139→    Save raw audio bytes to the cache and return the absolute file path.
   140→
   141→    Args:
   142→        data: Raw audio bytes.
   143→        ext:  File extension including the dot (e.g. ".ogg", ".mp3").
   144→
   145→    Returns:
   146→        Absolute path to the cached audio file as a string.
   147→    """
   148→    cache_dir = get_audio_cache_dir()
   149→    filename = f"audio_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}{ext}"
   150→    filepath = cache_dir / filename
   151→    filepath.write_bytes(data)
   152→    return str(filepath)
   153→
   154→
   155→async def cache_audio_from_url(url: str, ext: str = ".ogg") -> str:
   156→    """
   157→    Download an audio file from a URL and save it to the local cache.
   158→
   159→    Args:
   160→        url: The HTTP/HTTPS URL to download from.
   161→        ext: File extension including the dot (e.g. ".ogg", ".mp3").
   162→
   163→    Returns:
   164→        Absolute path to the cached audio file as a string.
   165→    """
   166→    import httpx
   167→
   168→    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
   169→        response = await client.get(
   170→            url,
   171→            headers={
   172→                "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; HermesAgent/1.0)",
   173→                "Accept": "audio/*,*/*;q=0.8",
   174→            },
   175→        )
   176→        response.raise_for_status()
   177→        return cache_audio_from_bytes(response.content, ext)
   178→

   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→# Document cache utilities
   182→#
   183→# Same pattern as image/audio cache -- documents from platforms are downloaded
   184→# here so the agent can reference them by local file path.
   185→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   186→
   187→DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/document_cache"))
   188→
   189→SUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPES = {
   190→    ".pdf": "application/pdf",
   191→    ".md": "text/markdown",
   192→    ".txt": "text/plain",
   193→    ".docx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
   194→    ".xlsx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
   195→    ".pptx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation",
   196→}
   197→
   198→
   199→def get_document_cache_dir() -> Path:
   200→    """Return the document cache directory, creating it if it doesn't exist."""
   201→    DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   202→    return DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR
   203→
   204→
   205→def cache_document_from_bytes(data: bytes, filename: str) -> str:
   206→    """
   207→    Save raw document bytes to the cache and return the absolute file path.
   208→
   209→    The cached filename preserves the original human-readable name with a
   210→    unique prefix: ``doc_{uuid12}_{original_filename}``.
   211→
   212→    Args:
   213→        data: Raw document bytes.
   214→        filename: Original filename (e.g. "report.pdf").
   215→
   216→    Returns:
   217→        Absolute path to the cached document file as a string.
   218→
   219→    Raises:
   220→        ValueError: If the sanitized path escapes the cache directory.
   221→    """
   222→    cache_dir = get_document_cache_dir()
   223→    # Sanitize: strip directory components, null bytes, and control characters
   224→    safe_name = Path(filename).name if filename else "document"
   225→    safe_name = safe_name.replace("\x00", "").strip()
   226→    if not safe_name or safe_name in (".", ".."):
   227→        safe_name = "document"
   228→    cached_name = f"doc_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}_{safe_name}"
   229→    filepath = cache_dir / cached_name
   230→    # Final safety check: ensure path stays inside cache dir
   231→    if not filepath.resolve().is_relative_to(cache_dir.resolve()):
   232→        raise ValueError(f"Path traversal rejected: {filename!r}")
   233→    filepath.write_bytes(data)
   234→    return str(filepath)
   235→
   236→
   237→def cleanup_document_cache(max_age_hours: int = 24) -> int:
   238→    """
   239→    Delete cached documents older than *max_age_hours*.
   240→
   241→    Returns the number of files removed.
   242→    """
   243→    import time
   244→
   245→    cache_dir = get_document_cache_dir()
   246→    cutoff = time.time() - (max_age_hours * 3600)
   247→    removed = 0
   248→    for f in cache_dir.iterdir():
   249→        if f.is_file() and f.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:
   250→            try:
   251→                f.unlink()
   252→                removed += 1
   253→            except OSError:
   254→                pass
   255→    return removed
   256→
   257→
   258→class MessageType(Enum):
   259→    """Types of incoming messages."""
   260→    TEXT = "text"
   261→    LOCATION = "location"
   262→    PHOTO = "photo"
   263→    VIDEO = "video"
   264→    AUDIO = "audio"
   265→    VOICE = "voice"
   266→    DOCUMENT = "document"
   267→    STICKER = "sticker"
   268→    COMMAND = "command"  # /command style
```

```python
        return

    self._loaded = True
```
